Here’s a quick rundown of the **federal long‑weekends** in Canada for 2023.  
(“Long‑weekend” means the holiday falls on a Monday or Friday, giving you a 3‑day break that includes the weekend.)

| Holiday | Date (2023) | Day of Week | Long‑Weekend? |
|---------|-------------|-------------|---------------|
| **Family Day** (Alberta, British Columbia, Saskatchewan, Ontario, New Brunswick, Manitoba, Prince Edward Island) | **Feb 20** | Monday | ✔️ (Fri‑Sat‑Sun‑Mon) |
| **Good Friday** | **Apr 7** | Friday | ✔️ (Fri‑Sat‑Sun) |
| **Victoria Day** | **May 22** | Monday | ✔️ (Fri‑Sat‑Sun‑Mon) |
| **Labour Day** | **Sep 4** | Monday | ✔️ (Fri‑Sat‑Sun‑Mon) |
| **Thanksgiving** | **Oct 9** | Monday | ✔️ (Fri‑Sat‑Sun‑Mon) |
| **Christmas** | **Dec 25** | Monday | ✔️ (Fri‑Sat‑Sun‑Mon) |

### Notes

| Holiday | 2023 Observance | Extra Info |
|---------|-----------------|------------|
| **Canada Day** | **Jul 1** (Saturday) | Falls on a weekend; no official long‑weekend unless you take a day off (many people observe a substitute day on Monday). |
| **Remembrance Day** | **Nov 11** (Saturday) | Same situation as Canada Day – no official long‑weekend. |
| **Boxing Day** | **Dec 26** (Tuesday) | Not a long‑weekend. |

> **Pro‑Tip:** If you’re planning trips, the holidays above are the ones that automatically give you a 3‑day break. For a more exhaustive list (including provincial holidays that create long‑weekends in specific provinces), you might want to consult the provincial holiday calendars or a dedicated holiday‑API.
